opportunities.title: Advanced JavaScript 1: Objects, Loops, Hoisting
opportunities.description:
This advanced JavaScript course deepens your understanding of key programming concepts, equipping you with the tools to write more efficient and scalable code. 

Through hands-on lessons and challenges, you’ll explore key JavaScript features like hoisting, loops, and object destructuring, along with ternary operators and asynchronous functions like setTimeout and setInterval.

You’ll also focus heavily on loops and methods for manipulating objects and arrays, gaining practical experience in modern function handling techniques such as arrow functions, default parameters, and callback functions.

This interactive course is designed to enhance your learning with coding challenges and real-world problem-solving tasks. You'll be writing, testing, and refining code throughout, ensuring that you not only understand the concepts but also have the practical skills to implement them in various scenarios.

By the end of this course, you will be able to solve complex challenges and apply best practices for structuring your code to handle real-world problems.

opportunities.description: Conducts routine analyses of samples in compliance with applicable methods, protocols, SOPs, and regulatory agency guidelines. Documents work, maintains study documentation, and laboratory records according to appropriate regulatory documentation practices.  Also can perform QC review of data. Operates laboratory equipment and system software appropriate for assigned tasks with assistance. May attend and provides input in project meetings. Informs Study Director, Lead Scientist, and/or management of any problems or deviations that may affect integrity of the data; participates in corrective action of problems. Contributes to a cohesive team environment.  Plans individual assigned workload on a daily basis in coordination with team members, can effectively manage multiple assignments. Assists in evaluating data and experiment modification as directed. Provides ideas, supports, and participates in process improvement initiatives. Maintains a clean and safe laboratory work environment.  Demonstrates understanding of Health and Safety compliance by ensuring that policies/SOPs and training are up to date. Performs other related duties as assigned. Bachelor of Science (BS) degree or college degree plus at least 2-year applicable experience. The degree can be in Chemistry, Biology or related field. Experience may be substituted for education. 0-2 years related or relevant laboratory experience required with a Associate or BS degree. opportunities.title: Goals in Action (GIA) - Fall 2026
opportunities.description:
Goals in Action (GIA) is a 6-week program centered on supporting undergraduate students as they develop and reach their academic goals. This program is intended for students who would like to develop greater academic resilience and skills, and is appropriate for students who are struggling academically, at risk or are on academic recovery plans, or at risk for dismissal.

Learn how you can use your strengths and resources to:
- Develop goals based on your values and align your actions accordingly, as values-driven action is more sustainable in the long run.
- Build healthy skills to manage stressors and your time effectively.
- Identify barriers and seek out support to help you succeed.

GIA program meets weekly for 6 weeks, with each section running 60 minutes. Sections are offered in-person and virtually.
---
